items.title: Dynamics 365 Contact Center: Use bullseye routing with user groups to orchestrate conversations
items.description:
Bullseye routing with user groups enables a tiered assignment strategy that automatically expands the pool of eligible representatives as conversation wait time increases. Rather than assigning from a fixed pool or waiting for overflow rules to trigger, this approach progressively widens availability in concentric rings—starting with the best-fit representatives and expanding outward as needed.

Administrators configure this scenario by associating user groups with a queue and defining wait time thresholds for each tier. For example:

  • 0–30 seconds: Assign to Tier 1 specialists (primary user group)
  • 30–60 seconds: Expand to include Tier 2 representatives (secondary user group)
  • 60+ seconds: Include all available representatives (tertiary user group)

Conversation orchestration monitors each conversation's wait time and automatically expands the eligible pool when thresholds are reached. This process ensures that customers are matched with the most qualified available representative, while preventing excessive wait times when the primary pool is at capacity.

Key benefits:

  • Best-fit first: Prioritizes the most qualified representatives before expanding to broader pools.
  • Automatic expansion: No manual intervention required—wait time thresholds trigger expansion automatically.
  • Configurable tiers: Define as many user group tiers as needed, with custom wait time thresholds for each.
  • Seamless integration: Works alongside other conversation orchestration scenarios like dynamic priority escalation and overflow based on representative availability.

items.title: Dynamics 365 Contact Center: Unified routing - Use overflow actions to protect customer experience for direct inward calls
items.description:
Overflow for direct inward dialing leverages conversation orchestration to detect key direct inward dialing-related events—such as the representative being busy, offline, rejecting the call, or failing to answer—and apply administrator-defined fallback actions.

Administrators configure natural language playbooks using conversation orchestration at the global or inbound profile level to specify the action to run when a direct inward dialed call can't be attended to or completed. The actions include offering a direct callback to the caller, sending them to voicemail, transferring the call to another queue or external number, or ending the call.

items.title: Dynamics 365 Contact Center: Unified routing - Orchestrate conversation distribution with natural language playbooks
items.description:
Conversation orchestration in Dynamics 365 Contact Center keeps every conversation actively managed throughout its lifecycle, from initiation through resolution. Instead of applying fixed rules at different stages of a conversation journey, conversation orchestration monitors each conversation as conditions evolve, like wait time increases, fast-filling queues, or service representatives going offline, and responds automatically with the right action. For example, administrators can define the intent using natural-language playbooks as follows: "If a premium customer waits for more than three minutes and no senior agents are available, increase their priority and offer a callback." Conversation orchestration then handles how it's run in real time.

You can configure playbooks per scenario through guided templates that keep instructions focused and reliable. Built-in validation catches conflicts before anything goes live, so that you confidently publish changes without needing to test every edge case manually.

The key capabilities are as follows:

  • Dynamic priority escalation: In traditional systems, conversation priority is typically set once, at entry, and never revisited. This means a customer who has been waiting for 10 minutes competes for the same expert as another customer who has just arrived, and a conversation that’s transferred mid-journey resets to whatever the new queue's default priority is. Dynamic priority escalation fixes this by continuously re-evaluating priority as the conversation progresses. You define the conditions such as wait time thresholds, queue transfers, customer tier, or other context and conversation orchestration adjusts priority automatically throughout the conversation lifecycle. High-value or long-waiting customers move forward without anyone watching the queue manually.

  • Overflow handling across multiple conditions: Conversation orchestration supports a broader set of business triggered overflow conditions, allowing organizations to respond intelligently as queue conditions change. Administrators can define actions when a queue is outside operating hours, when all representatives in a queue are signed out or unavailable, when queue wait time exceeds a defined threshold, or when the number of waiting conversations surpasses a specified limit. Depending on the situation, orchestration can automatically offer callbacks, route conversations to alternate queues, expand assignment eligibility, notify supervisors, or deliver contextual customer messages. This ensures customers are never left waiting without a defined path forward. Admins can also configure overflow handling for direct inward dial calls now, when reps are not available or don't accept the calls.

  • Assign to a previously engaged or preferred representative: Customers often need to repeat information when they are connected to a new representative for every interaction. Conversation orchestration helps maintain continuity by reconnecting customers with previously engaged or preferred representatives whenever possible. Assignment decisions take into account historical interactions, queue membership alignment, representative availability, and workload capacity. For asynchronous conversations, organizations can choose to honor representative presence status and active conversation limits before reconnecting customers, ensuring returning conversations are assigned only when the preferred representative has capacity to engage. When the preferred or previously engaged representative is unavailable, conversations seamlessly fall back to the next best qualified representative. This reduces customer effort, improves resolution efficiency, and delivers a more personalized support experience.

  • Bullseye routing: Finding the right representative often requires balancing expertise with response times. Bullseye routing enables organizations to gradually expand the pool of eligible representatives when a conversation isn't assigned within a defined timeframe. Administrators can define progressive routing rings that begin with the most qualified representatives and then expand to broader groups based on skills, proficiency levels, teams, or other business criteria. This approach maximizes the likelihood of connecting customers with the best-qualified representative while ensuring conversations don't wait indefinitely for a specific resource.

These capabilities are the first in a broad and growing set of orchestration scenarios that conversation orchestration will support across the full conversation lifecycle, spanning overflow management, priority handling, assignment strategies, in-conversation messaging, and escalation. Each new capability builds on the same natural-language playbook foundation, so organizations can adopt new scenarios without rebuilding what they have already configured.

Business Value:

Traditional automatic conversation distribution systems rely on complex rules and static configuration that are difficult to maintain and can't adapt as conditions change throughout the conversation lifecycle. Unified routing with its new AI-powered conversation orchestration uses the power of agentic AI to continuously monitor events throughout the entire conversation lifecycle and responds with the right action when required.

This is a shift from a static system to an orchestration layer that remains active and intelligent from the moment a conversation arrives in a queue until it's resolved. The new feature reduces administrative complexity and helps deliver more flexible customer experiences at scale, even under fluctuating demand.

Enabled for:

Enabled by admins/makers/marketers for end users

items.title: Dynamics 365 Contact Center: Unified routing - Handle waiting conversations when queues close or become unstaffed
items.description:
This capability enhances queue handling by intelligently detecting two key scenarios where conversations would otherwise remain unserved:

  • Queue transitions to out-of-operating hours: The system continuously monitors active conversations that entered a queue before closing time. If the queue transitions to out-of-operating hours while conversations are still waiting, it automatically applies admin-defined overflow actions. Customers can be guided to leave a voicemail, request a callback, or be transferred to another available queue, ensuring a smooth end-of-day experience without manual intervention.

  • No service representatives are signed in: The system evaluates real-time representative availability. If all representatives assigned to a queue are signed out, it immediately triggers the configured fallback action instead of waiting for in-queue overflow timers. This is especially valuable in scenarios such as mass logout events, unexpected breaks, or holidays not captured in operating hours.

Administrators configure both scenarios using natural language prompts in conversation orchestration, enabling fine-grained control over queue behavior. This ensures customers are always routed to the best possible outcome, even when direct support is unavailable.

Business Value:

This capability ensures customers are never left waiting when representatives aren't available. Whether a queue transitions to be out-of-operating hours or all support representatives are logged out, the system proactively routes conversations to configured fallback options such as voicemail, callback, or alternative queues.

Organizations benefit from reduced wait times and lower abandonment, improved customer satisfaction during peak load or unexpected staffing gaps, and a more predictable service experience regardless of representative availability. At the same time, this eliminates the need for manual queue draining or extended shifts, helping protect service representative wellbeing while maintaining consistent service levels.

Enabled for:

Enabled by admins/makers/marketers for end users

items.title: Dynamics 365 Contact Center: Unified routing - Assign conversation to expert who engaged with the customer previously
items.description:
Assign to a previously engaged or preferred expert leverages historical interaction context, queue membership alignment, and expert availability, to ensure customers are reconnected with experts who already understand their issue. When the previous or preferred expert is unavailable, assignments seamlessly fall back to the next best qualified expert, preserving service levels and reliability. This capability reduces repeat explanations, accelerates resolution times, and improves customer satisfaction, helping businesses lower cost to serve while delivering more consistent, personalized support experiences at scale. Administrators define assignment logic using natural language-based playbooks in conversation orchestration, with configurable lookback period to determine the time range until when the system should look for a previously engaged expert.

For asynchronous conversations, administrators can also choose to reconnect customers with the same expert by checking the expert’s current presence status and honoring active conversation limits, ensuring returning conversations are assigned only when the expert has capacity to engage.

Business Value:

By automatically assigning customers to a previous or preferred expert, you deliver faster, more personalized support. By routing repeat or follow up conversations to the most recent or preferred expert within configurable time windows, you reduce customer repetition, improve continuity, and accelerate resolution. When the previous expert is unavailable, the system intelligently falls back to the next best qualified expert, ensuring service levels are maintained. This leads to lower handling times, higher customer satisfaction, and improved expert efficiency.

Enabled for:

Enabled by admins/makers/marketers for end users

items.title: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Microsoft 365): Accounting skills
items.description:
Streamline corporate accounting work

New accounting capabilities in Excel and Cowork help accountants spend less time on repetitive, manual tasks in the places they already work, including:

• Reconcile accounts with confidence: Compare balances and transactions, identify discrepancies, and prepare reconciling items for review.

• Prepare journal entries faster: Draft accruals, reclassifications, allocations, reversals, and recurring entries, with checks for required inputs and balanced entries.

• Turn results into clear reporting: Analyze financial performance against plan, identify key drivers, and prepare reporting that explains what changed and why.

Additional capabilities span audit, tax, FP&A, compliance, and training. Learn more about the full set of accounting capabilities here.

Accountants are already putting these capabilities to work. In seven days of limited Insiders availability, more than 8,000 unique users invoked accounting skills over 44,000 times across more than 18,000 Copilot conversations.
Across Excel and Cowork, finance professionals will also have the option to start an audit trail whenever they invoke an accounting capability. If selected, this will create a record in their chat history of what Copilot changed and why. This is available today in Excel and coming soon to Cowork.

items.title: Dynamics 365 Commerce: Design POS screen layouts in a modern browser designer
items.description:
Create and preview POS screen layouts in headquarters with a modern web designer that simplifies configuration and reduces design iterations.

The Screen layout designer is modernized as a React-based web experience embedded in Commerce headquarters, with a JSON-based layout backbone replacing the legacy XML representation. The feature applies to Store Commerce point of sale (POS).

The modernization includes these core capabilities:

  • Visual layout and button-grid authoring: Arrange and resize supported POS components on a drag-and-drop canvas, configure properties, and edit associated button grids and POS operation mappings in a unified experience.
  • Live preview: Inspect layouts and their associated button-grid operations while designing, and preview supported device sizes and orientations without distributing every design iteration to stores.
  • Existing layout migration: Bring existing screen layouts and button-grid configurations into the modern designer rather than recreate them from scratch.
  • Reusable configuration: Reuse layout templates with store-specific overrides to reduce the need to maintain duplicate layouts.
  • Modern usability: Work with contextual properties, familiar Fluent UI controls, and inline validation.

Administrators enable or disable the modern designer through feature management in headquarters. Authorized users open Retail and Commerce > Channel setup > POS setup > POS > Screen layouts, select a layout, and open the designer. They configure the layout and button grids, inspect the preview, and save changes to headquarters. Administrators distribute the saved configuration to stores through the existing Commerce data distribution process. Previewing changes does not replace the distribution needed to update Store Commerce.

Setup is performed by a Commerce administrator, who enables the feature, grants appropriate headquarters permissions, and manages layout assignments and distribution. No separate ClickOnce designer installation or Copilot license is required for manual design.

items.title: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights - Journeys: Marketing tools, skills and plugin are now available in Copilot Cowork

Marketers and other customer-facing teams can understand customer profiles, author brand-compliant content, and prepare consent-aware outreach using existing segments directly in the flow of work, reducing the need to switch to Dynamics 365 Customer Insights.

The native Customer Insights skills (Customer Brief & Value Metrics, Email Content Advisor, and Customer Outreach) invoke tools published through the Dynamics 365 MCP server to retrieve unified customer profile and journey context and to perform supported actions in Customer Insights – Journeys. These tools respect Dynamics 365 business logic and the user's existing permissions on each call. The skills are included in the Customer Insights plugin, providing administrators with a governed way to deploy and manage the capabilities.

We’re expanding cost management for Microsoft Copilot Studio into the Microsoft 365 admin center. This gives administrators a more centralized way to manage Copilot Credit spend across usage-based AI workloads while retaining Copilot Studio cost management capabilities in the Power Platform admin center.
With this update, administrators can bring supported Copilot Studio environments and agents under Cost Management spending policies. Resource-based policies for environments and agents are the first planned scopes, with broader user and group policy support planned for a later phase.
Furthermore, this update will introduce cost data into cost management and agent registry for AI services and agents built on Microsoft platforms (e.g., Cowork, Microsoft Copilot Studio agents).

items.title: Dynamics 365 Customer Service: Shared analytics foundation for historical reporting
items.description: Dynamics 365 Customer Service provides out-of-the-box historical reporting built on a shared analytics foundation: a scalable, open, and AI-ready data foundation for Customer Experience and AI analytics scenarios across Dynamics 365. It uses a lakehouse-based architecture that can scale with data volume, supports curated analytics datasets for direct querying, and enables consistent reporting and semantic definitions across reports, agents, and copilots.

items.title: Outlook: All Accounts view (Unified Inbox) brings your email into a single inbox view
items.description: The All-Accounts view, also known as Unified Inbox, lets you see emails from multiple accounts in a single inbox view in the new Outlook for Windows, without merging your mailboxes. Each account's inbox stays separate; the view brings them together so you can triage in one place. Users can read, delete, move, archive, and mark messages across accounts without switching between mailboxes. The experience integrates with Copilot for AI-assisted email workflows and supports Immersive Search for finding messages across your primary account. Advanced scenarios such as cross-account search and shared mailbox support will follow in later releases.

items.title: Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): Copilot Chat in Outlook expands to reason over inbox, calendar, and enterprise data
items.description: Copilot Chat in Outlook expanding to support reasoning over a user's entire inbox, calendar and other enterprise data for Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat users (without a Microsoft 365 Copilot license) .

items.title: Microsoft Purview: Data Lifecycle Management-Legacy Teams retention policies covering Copilot will be treated as Teams-only
items.description: Some existing retention policies scoped to Microsoft Teams may currently also apply to Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions. As part of an upcoming change, these legacy Teams retention policies will be converted to—and treated as—Teams-only policies. They will no longer implicitly govern Copilot workloads.

items.title: Microsoft Copilot Studio: Agent Sharing amongst makers
items.description: Enables sharing of agents with other makers in the new Microsoft Copilot harness. Makers can grant other makers Agent Viewer (view analytics/evaluations only) or Editor (view, edit, configure, share, publish) access to an agent, with auto-assigned security roles.

items.title: Microsoft Edge: Ask Copilot about an image
items.description: Ask Copilot about an image in Edge enables users to instantly analyze images from the web by sending them directly to Copilot from the Edge context menu, making it easy to ask questions, gain insights, and understand visual content without leaving their browsing experience. Admins can control availability to this feature using the EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext and Microsoft365CopilotChatIconEnabled policies.
